title: ProtoXTM: Cross-Lingual Topic Modeling with Document-Level Prototype-based Contrastive Learning
subcategory: cross-lingual NTM with document-level prototype contrastive learning
task: Discovering aligned, interpretable topics in bilingual (English-Chinese) corpora
problem: Word-level dictionary alignment causes topic mismatch (translation pairs that are not topically coherent) and degrades intra-lingual topic interpretability.
architecture: Stage 1: a monolingual CTM per language gives pseudo cluster labels (argmax topic). Stage 2: retrieval-based positive sampling translates each topic's top words with an M2M NMT model (out-of-vocabulary words replaced by FastText neighbours) and retrieves target-language positives with BM25. Stage 3: document-level prototype-based contrastive learning on topic-cluster prototypes in a shared latent space, with one decoder per language.
llm_or_encoder: CTM (contextualised embeddings); M2M neural machine translation; FastText; BM25
key_results: ECNews, 10 topics: CNPMI 0.0717 vs 0.0370 for InfoCTM; Amazon Review: CNPMI 0.0564 vs 0.0455 for NMTM.
CNPMI improves by up to 93.8% over cross-lingual baselines; ECNews Purity 0.6204 vs 0.5832 for NMTM.
strengths: Protects intra-lingual interpretability by pre-training monolingual models before alignment.
Positive sampling without data augmentation; prototype-level contrast is cheaper than instance-level contrast.

limitations.text: Sensitivity to the choice of machine-translation model is not investigated.
Evaluated only on English-Chinese; truly low-resource languages remain open.
Many hyper-parameters need empirical tuning; the number of topics is unresolved.
Evaluated with small topic numbers (10 and 20).

notes: Mean of five runs; implemented with TopMost.
